sentences.text: Heard on IA No.2726/2019, an application moved on behalf of appellant under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay.
2. On due consideration and for the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed.
Delay of 37 days in filing the instant appeal, is hereby condoned.

3. This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 18.02.2019 passed by the XI Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Gwalior (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 105/2016, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11400 2 MA-3636-2019 5.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to permanent disability sustained by Vinod Singh in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,92,000/-
along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellant/claimant has preferred this appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal passed the award without proper appreciation of law.
It is contended that the compensation awarded is on the lower side.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the appellant clearly establishes that prior to the accident, the appellant was a healthy 24-year-old person and was engaged in labour work, earning Rs. 9,000/- per month.
However, the learned Claims Tribunal failed to consider these aspects and assessed the income of the appellant at Rs. 3,000/- per month, which is extremely low.

It is further submitted that due to the accident, the appellant sustained grievous injuries to his right leg, and during the course of treatment, his right leg was amputated above the knee but not beyond middle thigh, resulting in 80% permanent disability of the right leg.
Due to the said disability, the appellant is unable to do any work and has suffered 100% loss of earning capacity for the rest of his life.
However, the learned Claims Tribunal erred in not awarding compensation on the basis of 100% loss of earning capacity.
The appellant also suffered severe physical and mental pain during treatment, incurred substantial medical expenses, and has been rendered incapable of pursuing his vocation for his entire life.

Despite this,
the Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of only Rs. 3,92,000/- under all heads, which is grossly inadequate.
Hence, it is prayed that a just and reasonable amount of compensation be awarded.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No. 3/Insurance Company supported the impugned award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11400 3 MA-3636-2019 has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record.

entities.text:
Claims Tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11400 3 MA-3636-2019
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and deserves to be dismissed.

8 . Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
9.

On going through the evidence, including the medical evidence and the amputation certificate of the claimant, it is clear that the right leg of the claimant was amputated above the knee but not beyond the middle thigh in the alleged accident.

As per Schedule I, Part II (18) of the Employees'
Compensation Act, the permanent disability is assessed at 70%.
However, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation only to the tune of Rs. 3,92,000/-, which is not correct in the eyes of law.
Hence, for calculating the compensation, 70% of permanent disability, be assessed.
10. Further, on perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the claimant has utterly failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the claimant.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the claimant as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases o f Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways, 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.

sentences.text: Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the claimant as an unskilled person as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.3,995/- per month.

sentences.text:
As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:11400 4 MA-3636-2019 o f National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimant is entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% be assessed.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the claimant is to be taken into account, multiplier of 17 be applied.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr.
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Looking to the injuries sustained by the claimant, loss of earning during treatment,,
mental agony, pain & suffering, special diet, attendant and travelling, etc. due to the alleged accident, this Court thinks it appropriate to enhance Rs.2,00,000/- under these heads.
Further, the claims Tribunal has awarded compensation in the head of medical expenses to the tune of Rs.39,000/-, is just and proper, needs no interference.

12. Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   
 Income  
 Future Prospects @ 40% 
 Permanent disability @ 70% 
 Multiplier 17   Loss of earning of three months
during treatment

Medical expenses  Other Heads i.e.pain & suffering, special diet, attendant Rs.2,00,000/-
and travelling, etc.

Total Compensation = Rs.10,49,662/-
13.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.10,49,662/- as against the sum of Rs.3,92,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.6,57,662/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:11400 5 MA-3636-2019 claims Tribunal.
14.
Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.6,57,662/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellant/claimant within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

15. In case, the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellant shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
